title: The Paper Orchard
premise: In the final winter of the Republic of Vessany, Odile Nystrom carries sealed diplomatic codes through a capital already being carved up by the victors' commissions. When an unknown woman leaves a child on his doorstep with a note reading 'forget my face,' he recognizes her as the archivist who once showed him the republic's true surrender terms — terms that were never published. Pursued by both the retreating loyalists and the new regime's historians, Odile must decide whether the child is a burden, a trap, or the last living witness to what was actually signed. He smuggles the boy and the original documents to a neutral printing house, getting the truth on record hours before the victors burn the archive, though it costs him his name, his safety, and any claim to the life he had.
about_author: Orsen Quintana is the pen name of a former archival clerk who spent a decade cataloging the confiscated papers of collapsed governments before turning to fiction. They write from a small coastal town, where they keep an orchard of paper-mulberry trees grown from cuttings of uncertain provenance.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Things
chapters.summary: Odile Nystrom, POV: On the republic's last functioning morning, Odile delivers final coded orders across a capital of shuttered ministries, measuring his world in what fits in a courier's satchel. At night, a woman leaves a child at his door with instructions to forget her face — and he recognizes her voice. The beat is dread disguised as routine; the ordinary world cracks open.

chapters.title: What the Archivist Knew
chapters.summary: Odile's POV: Following the note's cipher to a flooded records annex, Odile reconstructs why the archivist chose him: he carried the courier copy of the secret capitulation terms that contradict everything the victors now publish. Victors' historians begin canvassing couriers by name. The emotional beat shifts from fear to complicity — he realizes he has been carrying the lie for months without knowing it.

chapters.title: The Burning Season
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, with interludes in the child's fragmentary memory: As the victors torch the state archives, Odile races to move the original documents and the boy through checkpoints, betrayed by a fellow courier who has already sold the route. The climax comes at the neutral printing house, where typesetters set the true terms as soldiers breach the door — truth committed to ink with minutes to spare.

chapters.title: A Name Left Behind
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, years later: Under a borrowed identity in another country, Odile reads the suppressed terms circulating in samizdat copies and watches the victors' official history quietly amended. He gives the boy, now settled, one honest answer about the face he was told to forget. The resolution is bittersweet: the record survives, but its keeper remains unrecorded — inheritance passed on without a signature.
